description:
FOUND s501b (Opus, 2026-09-30) re-attributing the everyday row modules/IO-Select-Socket (its cause #1998 is completed).  PRE-EXISTING: main 77212b1f (base extraction) behaves identically.  s501b added the missing `PF_UNSPEC` to lib/Socket.pm (the program died "Undefined subroutine &main::PF_UNSPEC" before reaching either bug); the row now differs at line 1 with `0  port hello from child …` where perl prints `1 ping port hello from child …` -- i.e. can_read found nothing and the sysread never ran.

TWO bugs, both on the select+sysread path, probes in the s501b worktree scratch/s501b/p/:

(1) sel1.pl / sel2.pl -- `pipe(my $r,my $w); syswrite($w,"x\n"); vec($rin,fileno($r),1)=1; select($rout=$rin,undef,undef,1)` -> perl 1, PCL 0 (pipe AND socketpair; IO::Select->can_read therefore returns ()).
CAUSE (read, not guessed): %p-select-4arg calls `sb-unix:unix-fast-select` with INTEGER fd masks, but that function takes pointers to alien `fd_set`s (its lambda list is num-descriptors read-fds write-fds exception-fds secs usecs, and SBCL's compiler warns "Derived type of (ASH 1 R) … conflicting with its asserted type" when fed an integer).  The call signals, and the surrounding `(handler-case … (error () 0))` turns it into "0 ready" -- a rule-12 violation (a value the program consumes, silently wrong).  FIX SHAPE: `(sb-alien:with-alien ((rfds (sb-alien:struct sb-unix:fd-set)) …) (sb-unix:fd-zero rfds) (sb-unix:fd-set fd rfds) … (sb-unix:unix-fast-select n (sb-alien:addr rfds) …) (sb-unix:fd-isset fd rfds))` -- the pattern SBCL's own serve-event uses; and the error arm must set $! and return -1 (perl's failure value), never 0.  Probably also the cause of #1934 (4-arg select "rejects a plain string" -- op/sselect.t 3 rows): re-probe it after the fix.

(2) sp1.pl / sp3.pl -- `syswrite($w, "ping\n"); sysread($r, my $buf, 100)` on a pipe or a socketpair: perl returns 5 at once; PCL BLOCKS FOREVER (timeout 20 s, rc 124).
CAUSE: %p-sysread-impl is `(%p-read-impl …)` "same as read for now", and %p-read-impl uses `read-sequence`, which waits until LENGTH characters or EOF.  perl's sysread is ONE read(2): it returns whatever is available (at least 1 byte, or 0 at EOF).  FIX SHAPE: sysread on an fd-backed stream reads the descriptor once (sb-unix:unix-read into a byte buffer, then the stream's decoding), after draining anything already in the Lisp stream's input buffer; `read` keeps read-sequence (perl's buffered read does loop).

ACCEPTANCE: everyday/modules/IO-Select-Socket == perl; sel1.pl sel2.pl sp1.pl sp3.pl == perl.  BAR: cl/ => full sweep + companion io/ (io/select.t, io/sem.t, op/sselect.t) BEFORE/AFTER; guard rows in Pl/t/socket-01.t.

=== DONE (s502e, Opus, 2026-10-04) ===
SHIPPED (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp + Pl/ExprToCL.pm):
(1) 4-arg select: each defined mask's bytes become a real fd_set (perl's vec() layout IS the fd_set layout on a little-endian host; buffers rounded to 8 bytes), select(2) is called through sb-alien with NULL for an undef mask/timeout, nfds = 8 x the longest mask, every defined mask is written back whatever the count (cleared bits included), list context returns (NFOUND, TIMELEFT) -- `select` joined %WANTARRAY_SENSITIVE so a list-context bind cannot leak -- and a failing select(2) returns -1 with $! (rule 12: never 0).  The timeout and each mask are FETCHed exactly once (RT#120102 -- the companion op/sselect.t caught the first version FETCHing twice); a wide character in a mask dies `Wide character...`.  The sleep form (no masks) is the same call with nfds 0.
(2) sysread: %p-read-impl takes the reader as an argument; sysread's reader blocks for the first character (0 at EOF) and then takes only what read-char-no-hang has, up to LEN; a regular file (fstat S_ISREG) keeps read-sequence.  Offset/EBADF/negative-length handling is read's, unchanged.
Normative: ir-spec §7.6a.
PROBES (scratch/s502e/p/): sel.pl (pipe + socketpair, ready / not ready / timeout 0 / 0.2 / 1 / undef, write mask, both masks, count, timeleft in list ctx, EOF, bad fd), sel3.pl (timeouts 0/0.3/1/1.5 s accurate), sel5.pl (scalar ctx inside a list-context sub), sr.pl (partial pipe read, short read, OFFSET +/-, NUL padding, EOF 0 twice, closed handle undef + errno, socketpair partial/short/rest, regular file 4096/904/0) == perl; base returns 0 for every select and HANGS on sysread.  NOT modelled: perl's sysread after a buffered readline on the same pipe BLOCKS (the data sits in PerlIO's buffer); PCL returns the buffered data -- dropped from the probe (perl hangs).
COMPANION: io/ (44 files, --jobs 1 --quick) identical before/after; op/sselect.t 17/6 -> 20/3 (the three wide-character rows FIXED, edited out of perl-suite-fails.tsv; rows 10-12 = a literal mask is read-only, #1934, unchanged); op/sysio.t OK 45/0 and op/select.t 3/6 both unchanged.
EVERYDAY: modules/IO-Select-Socket `same` (row edited out).
corpus-diff: readline.t + scalar.t differ ONLY by `(p-scalar-ctx (p-select …))` around a 1-arg select (the wantarray-sensitive bind); emission-ab lib/: IO.pm and IO/Handle.pm the same class.
GUARD: Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t rows 81-82 (each program starts `alarm 30`: the base hung on them) + 85 (tied timeout fetched once, wide mask dies); all inverse-verified failing on the 618db500 extraction.
subject: 4-arg select NEVER reports a ready descriptor (integer masks handed to sb-unix:unix-fast-select, the type error swallowed as 0), and sysread BLOCKS for the full LENGTH on a pipe/socket instead of returning what is available -- IO::Select->can_read and every select+sysread loop are dead
